title: DFT geometry optimization
action: Perform DFT geometry optimization for bulk β‑Ga₂O₃ and hydrogen‑passivated 2D monoclinic Ga₂O₃ slabs (monolayer, bilayer, trilayer) using an open-source DFT code with the LDA functional. For 2D systems, add a vacuum layer of at least 15 Å. Relax cell parameters and atomic positions until forces are converged (typical threshold < 0.001 eV/Å).
description: Obtain the equilibrium lattice constants and atomic positions needed for elastic constant calculations. The relaxed structures can be saved as a text log for evidence.

title: Elastic constants, moduli, sound velocities, Debye temperature and k_min
action: Using the optimized structures, compute the full set of thirteen independent elastic constants Cij for each thickness (bulk, monolayer, bilayer, trilayer) with the stress‑strain method within an open‑source DFT code. Apply the Voigt–Reuss–Hill averaging scheme to obtain polycrystalline moduli: bulk modulus B, shear modulus G, Young's modulus E, and Poisson's ratio ν. Compute mass density ρ from cell volume and atomic masses. From E, ν, and ρ, calculate the longitudinal (vl), transverse (vt), and average (vm) sound velocities using effective‑medium acoustic relations. Then compute the Debye temperature ΘD using the appropriate 2D or 3D formula (involving vm, number of atoms per cell, and atomic area/volume). Finally, compute the minimum thermal conductivity k_min using a semi‑empirical formula that depends on Young's modulus, mass density, unit‑cell mass, and atom count. Report all quantities (Cij, B, G, E, ν, vl, vt, vm, ΘD, k_min, and the saturated isochoric heat capacity C_V_saturated obtained from the Debye temperature) for each thickness in a single JSON file.
description: JSON file containing, for each thickness (bulk, monolayer, bilayer, trilayer), the elastic constants, derived moduli, sound velocities, Debye temperature, minimum thermal conductivity, and saturated heat capacity. The checker will compare these values to hidden reference values (the paper's reported numbers) within tolerances and verify required ordering trends.
output_schema: A JSON object with keys 'bulk', 'monolayer', 'bilayer', 'trilayer'. Each value is an object containing: 'elastic_constants' (object with keys C11..C66, C12, C13, C15, C23, C25, C35, C46; values are numbers in units GPa for bulk and N/m for 2D), 'B' (number, GPa or N/m accordingly), 'G' (number, same unit), 'E' (number, same unit), 'nu' (number, dimensionless), 'vl' (number, units m/s), 'vt' (number, units m/s), 'vm' (number, units m/s), 'Theta_D' (number, units K), 'k_min' (number, units W·cm⁻¹·K⁻¹), 'C_V_saturated' (number, units J·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹).

title: Specific heat capacity C_V(T)
action: Using the Debye temperature ΘD obtained in the previous step, compute the isochoric specific heat capacity C_V as a function of temperature for each system using the Debye model. Generate a CSV file with columns: thickness (string, one of 'bulk','monolayer','bilayer','trilayer'), temperature_K (float, temperature in Kelvin), and C_V_J_mol_K (float, heat capacity in J·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹). Cover the temperature range from approximately 0 K up to at least 1000 K with a fine enough mesh to show the approach to saturation.
description: CSV file with temperature‑dependent specific heat capacity curves for all four systems. The checker will verify that the high‑temperature saturated C_V values match the hidden reference within tolerance and that the curves follow a Debye‑like rise.
output_schema: CSV with header: thickness, temperature_K, C_V_J_mol_K. 'thickness' is one of 'bulk','monolayer','bilayer','trilayer'; 'temperature_K' is a positive float; 'C_V_J_mol_K' is a float ≥ 0.
